Your objective is the company's total profit across all six events. For this event, profit is the price you win at minus your total cost at your delivery and quality. Losing earns nothing. - Event 4 (speed-weighted contract): we were a quality specialist. We bid $134.00, 3 weeks, tier 2 in the final round and lost to the other supplier.

The pattern: on speed-weighted contracts the buyer rewards delivery time far more than quality tier. On quality-weighted contracts it rewards tier. Our winning final bids have been between about $117.50 and $126.00, and each carried a profit of $8.80 to $14.80. Our one loss came at $134.00. Price discipline has mattered more than extra terms.

HOW TO IDENTIFY THE CONTRACT

The contract is not named at the start. Use the platform's round 1 and round 2 replies to work out which dimension the buyer weights most. The platform has described the buyer's dominant dimension in past events, and it will likely do so again. If it says delivery speed dominates, the buyer is speed-weighted. If it says quality dominates, the buyer is quality-weighted. Do not spend cost on the lesser dimension.

THE OTHER SUPPLIER

The other supplier is usually of the opposite cost type to ours (about three events in four). If you are a speed specialist, expect the rival to be a quality specialist, which tends to offer higher tiers and slower delivery. If you are a quality specialist, expect the rival to be a speed specialist, which can beat you on delivery when speed is weighted heavily. The rival's replies and bids in rounds 1 and 2 are your best evidence of its position.

HOW TO USE THE THREE ROUNDS

- Round 1: Make a probing bid that is priced to win on the dominant dimension while keeping a clear margin over your cost. Do not drop to your floor yet.

Do not cut price below what keeps a healthy profit margin just because a reply recommends it. Price cuts should be earned by a real position gap on the dominant dimension. Check every suggestion against your own cost and margin.
